skill.name: image-audit
skill.description: Audits local images for adult, political, and violent content through an external MCP moderation service, then summarizes the results.
skill.summary: Compress image batches, submit them for content moderation, and review pass, blocked, and failed results.
skill.author: xiaowu89

security_audit.summary: Most static command and reconnaissance findings are Markdown or JavaScript syntax false positives. Confirmed risks include secret exposure, global package installation, external image transfer, unsafe value interpolation, and unbounded image processing.

remediation.issue: Local images are uploaded without an explicit transfer checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination and file count, then require user confirmation immediately before any upload.

remediation.issue: Paths, endpoints, and secrets are inserted into executable JavaScript literals.
remediation.suggestion: Pass values through validated arguments or environment variables, and parse configuration with a JSON parser.

remediation.issue: The workflow prints complete MCP configuration files.
remediation.suggestion: Read only the nx-mcp-audit entry and never place API key values in model context or logs.

remediation.issue: Image decoding and batch accumulation have no resource limits.
remediation.suggestion: Restore Sharp pixel limits and enforce file-count, input-byte, output-byte, and batch-size limits.

remediation.issue: The skill automatically installs an unpinned global npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Declare a pinned dependency and request confirmation before installation. Avoid modifying the global npm environment.

remediation.issue: Localized files configure different remote service endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Use one verified endpoint source and keep endpoint, author, and version metadata consistent across translations.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Values Embedded in Executable JavaScript
semantic_findings.description: Image paths, the endpoint, and the API key replace single-quoted placeholders. A crafted value containing a quote can inject JavaScript into the heredoc.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly requires direct placeholder replacement inside executable single-quoted JavaScript literals, with no escaping or structured argument passing.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Image Processing Can Exhaust Memory
semantic_findings.description: The script processes every matching file, disables Sharp pixel limits, and retains compressed data twice. Large batches or decompression bombs can exhaust memory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code has no file-count or byte limit, sets limitInputPixels to false, and stores each data URL in both records and data_urls.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Image Upload Without Explicit Transfer Consent
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends compressed local image contents to an external service. It does not require confirmation after naming the destination and selected files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both workflows direct the agent to encode local images and submit them externally, but neither requires informed confirmation immediately before transfer.

semantic_findings.title: Localized Instructions Use Different Remote Endpoints
semantic_findings.description: The Chinese and English files configure different hardcoded ModelScope endpoint identifiers. Users can send the same images to different service instances by language.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint strings visibly differ at the same configuration line in the two files, while both are presented as the nx-mcp-audit service.

content.value_statement: Manual image review is slow and inconsistent. This skill compresses image batches, submits them to an MCP moderation service, and summarizes pass, blocked, and failed results.
actual_capabilities: Processes one image or scans supported images in a selected folder.
Compresses images to a 500-pixel maximum edge with JPEG quality 40.
Converts compressed images into data URLs for MCP submission.
Calls the nx_img_audit MCP tool with image batches and an API key.
Summarizes pass, blocked, and failed results in a readable table.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or later, Sharp, network access, and an nx-mcp-audit API key.
Sends image contents and credentials to an external MCP service.
Moderation accuracy and availability depend on the external service.
The primary workflow lacks strict image-count, input-size, and decoded-pixel limits.

use_cases.title: Review User Uploads
use_cases.description: Screen a controlled batch of uploaded images before publication and identify items needing human review.

use_cases.title: Check Product Assets
use_cases.description: Audit local product images before release and summarize blocked or failed files for remediation.

use_cases.title: Triage Media Libraries
use_cases.description: Create a first-pass moderation report for a legacy image collection before detailed manual inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the image at [path]. Show the external destination and ask for confirmation before uploading it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one known local image

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Find supported images in [folder]. Report the file count, request upload confirmation, then return a moderation table.
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine review of a small image folder

prompt_templates.title: Review Selected Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit only these files: [file list]. Use batches of [size], retry failures once, and separate blocked results from service errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Controlled batch review with explicit scope

prompt_templates.title: Run a Constrained Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [folder] with a maximum of [count] files and [bytes] total input. Stop on limits and provide a manual-review queue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit with resource and workflow controls

output_examples.input: Audit one confirmed image after approving the external upload.
output_examples.output: Audit complete: product-front.jpg passed. The service returned no violation details.

output_examples.input: Audit a folder containing three supported images.
Audit a batch with one unreadable file.
output_examples.output: Processed four files: two passed, one blocked, and one failed during compression. The failed file was not uploaded.

best_practices: Confirm the destination and selected files immediately before external transfer.
Use small, bounded batches and enforce decoded-pixel and total-byte limits.
Treat blocked results as review signals and inspect failures separately.
anti_patterns: Do not print API keys or complete MCP configuration files.
Do not upload private images without informed user approval.
Do not treat automated moderation as a final legal or policy decision.

faq.question: What content can this skill detect?
faq.answer: The service reports adult, political, and violent content classifications.

faq.question: Does processing remain local?
faq.answer: No. Compression is local, but compressed image data is sent to an external MCP service.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need Node.js 18 or later, Sharp, network access, the MCP service, and a valid API key.

faq.question: Which image formats are supported?
faq.answer: The primary workflow lists PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, and TGA files.

faq.question: Can it audit image URLs?
faq.answer: The English workflow supports URLs, but recommends downloading and submitting compressed data URLs.

faq.question: Should blocked images be deleted automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review blocked images manually before removal because automated classifications can be incomplete or incorrect.
